title: Rhetoric and style
summary: Metaphor, litote, chiasmus and other classic devices: name them in Spanish, spot them in a short passage, and judge which register each one helps or hurts.
focus: Recognising and using rhetorical devices (metáfora, símil, hipérbole, lítote, eufemismo, antítesis, anáfora, quiasmo, hipérbaton, enumeración de tres, pregunta retórica) in the right register
content:
## Images: metáfora, símil, hipérbole

A **metáfora** names one thing as another, with no comparison word: **Esa reunión fue un pantano** (that meeting was a swamp). A **símil** keeps the comparison in view with **como**, **igual que** or **parecer**: **Hablaba despacio, como quien cuenta monedas** (he spoke slowly, like someone counting coins). A **hipérbole** exaggerates on purpose: **Llevo un siglo esperando** (I've been waiting for ages).

- Everyday Spanish is full of dead metaphors (**la pata de la mesa**, **el pie de página**) and stock hyperbole (**me muero de hambre**, **te lo he dicho mil veces**).
- A fresh image persuades; a worn one (**un mar de dudas**) makes prose sound second-hand.

## Saying less: lítote and eufemismo

The **lítote** (also **lítotes**) affirms by denying the opposite:

- **No es poco** = it is a lot.
- **No está nada mal** = it is very good.
- **No es ningún tonto** = he is sharp.

It sounds modest, warm or drily ironic, so it suits a review as well as a chat.

The **eufemismo** softens a hard word: **fallecer** or **se nos fue** for **morir**, **persona mayor** for **viejo**, **reajuste de plantilla** for **despidos**. It helps courtesy (a condolence card, a doctor's letter). It hurts when it hides a fact the reader needs: forty dismissals are still forty dismissals.

## Patterns: antítesis, quiasmo, anáfora and threes

| Device | What it does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **antítesis** | sets opposites side by side | **Mucho texto y poca idea.** (Lots of text, little idea.) |
| **quiasmo** | repeats a pair in reverse order: A B, B A | **Comemos tarde porque dormimos poco, y dormimos poco porque comemos tarde.** (We eat late because we sleep little, and vice versa.) |
| **anáfora** | repeats the opening word of each clause | **Sin luz, sin agua, sin respuesta.** (No light, no water, no answer.) |
| **enumeración de tres** | three parallel items that close a thought | **Claro, breve y amable.** (Clear, brief and kind.) |

These patterns suit speeches, columns and adverts. In an e-mail, one is plenty.

## Order and questions: hipérbaton and pregunta retórica

The **hipérbaton** breaks the usual word order for emphasis or rhythm:

- Neutral: **Recuerdo poco de aquel verano.**
- Hyperbaton: **De aquel verano, poco recuerdo.** (Of that summer, little do I remember.)

In prose a fronted complement sounds literary; pushed further, it sounds like parody.

The **pregunta retórica** asks what nobody needs to answer, to draw the reader in or to make a point:

- **¿Quién no ha perdido nunca las llaves?** (Everyone has.)
- **¿Hace falta decir más?** (No, it doesn't.)

One per page persuades; three in a row sound like a lecture.

## Register: when a device helps or hurts

| Register | Where | Devices at home there |
|---|---|---|
| **culto** | essays, speeches, literature | hipérbaton, quiasmo, antítesis, anáfora |
| **estándar** | the press, reports, e-mail | lítote, eufemismo, one well-placed metáfora |
| **coloquial** | talk, chats, messages | hipérbole, símil, pregunta retórica |

The test is fit. A hyperbole livens a conversation and undermines a report. A euphemism comforts in a condolence letter and misleads in a balance sheet. A word from the wrong register **chirría** (jars): **estirar la pata** (kick the bucket) has no place in an obituary, and **fallecer** sounds stiff in a chat with friends.

vocabulary.meaning: metaphor: one thing named as another, with no comparison word
vocabulary.example: Para la directora, el presupuesto es un cinturón que aprieta cada año.
vocabulary.example_meaning: For the director, the budget is a belt that tightens every year.

vocabulary.meaning: simile: a comparison made visible with como, igual que or parecer
vocabulary.example: Las ideas le salían como agua de una fuente rota.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Ideas came out of him like water from a broken fountain.

vocabulary.meaning: hyperbole: deliberate exaggeration
vocabulary.example: Decir que llevas un siglo esperando es una hipérbole.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Saying you've been waiting a century is hyperbole.

vocabulary.meaning: litotes: affirming by denying the opposite (no es poco, no está nada mal)
vocabulary.example: Ganar tres premios en un año no es poco.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Winning three prizes in a year is no small thing.

vocabulary.meaning: euphemism: a soft word for a hard thing
vocabulary.example: Llamar reajuste de plantilla a cuarenta despidos es un eufemismo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Calling forty dismissals a staff adjustment is a euphemism.

vocabulary.meaning: antithesis: opposites set side by side
vocabulary.example: La novela vive de una antítesis: el pueblo calla y la ciudad grita.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The novel lives on an antithesis: the village is silent and the city shouts.

vocabulary.meaning: chiasmus: a pair repeated in reverse order (A B, B A)
vocabulary.example: Hay un quiasmo en su lema: ni trabajo sin descanso ni descanso sin trabajo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There is a chiasmus in her motto: neither work without rest nor rest without work.

vocabulary.meaning: anaphora: the same word repeated at the start of each clause
vocabulary.example: Cada párrafo empezaba con queremos: una anáfora que acabó cansando.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Every paragraph began with 'we want': an anaphora that ended up wearing thin.

vocabulary.meaning: the rule of three: three parallel items that close a thought
vocabulary.example: Cerró la reseña con una enumeración de tres: puntual, limpio y barato.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She closed the review with a list of three: punctual, clean and cheap.

vocabulary.meaning: hyperbaton: a change of the usual word order for emphasis or rhythm
vocabulary.example: Con un hipérbaton abría el capítulo: de aquella casa, nada quedaba.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He opened the chapter with a hyperbaton: of that house, nothing remained.

vocabulary.meaning: rhetorical question: one asked to make a point, not to get an answer
vocabulary.example: ¿Quién lee hoy las instrucciones? Era una pregunta retórica, claro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Who reads the instructions these days? It was a rhetorical question, of course.

vocabulary.meaning: register: the level of a text (culto, estándar, coloquial)
vocabulary.example: En un informe, el registro coloquial resta credibilidad.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In a report, a colloquial register undermines credibility.

vocabulary.meaning: to grate, to jar (of a word or phrase that does not fit)
vocabulary.example: En una carta de pésame, cualquier broma chirría.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In a condolence letter, any joke jars.

quiz.prompt: Which device is this? «La sala se vació como una bañera sin tapón.»
quiz.explanation: Como makes the comparison visible, so it is a simile. Without como (La sala era una bañera sin tapón) it would be a metaphor.

quiz.prompt: Praising a colleague's report with a litote: Tu informe no está ___ mal.
quiz.explanation: No está nada mal denies the opposite to mean 'it is really quite good'. No está tan mal would only mean 'it isn't that bad'.
hints: A four-letter word meaning 'not at all'.

quiz.prompt: «Lo que el jefe dice, no lo hace; lo que hace, no lo dice.» What shapes this sentence?
quiz.explanation: Dice … hace, then hace … dice. The pair comes back in reverse order (A B, B A), which is a chiasmus.
hints: Compare the order of the two verbs in each half.

quiz.prompt: Calling a price rise «una actualización de tarifas» is a ___ (Spanish term).
quiz.explanation: A soft, technical phrase stands in for an unwelcome fact (prices go up). That is a euphemism.
hints: It softens; it does not exaggerate.

quiz.prompt: «Sin prisa, sin ruido, sin miedo, la alcaldesa cruzó la plaza y abrió el mercado.» Which device opens this passage?
quiz.explanation: Sin is repeated at the start of each phrase, which is anaphora. The three phrases also make an enumeración de tres before the main clause.
hints: Which word comes back at the start of each phrase?

quiz.prompt: Neutral order: No sabíamos nada de su viaje. With hyperbaton: De su viaje, nada ___.
quiz.explanation: The complement (de su viaje) and the object (nada) move in front of the verb for emphasis; the verb stays the same: sabíamos.
hints: The verb moves to the end.

quiz.prompt: A question asked to make a point, not to get an answer, is a pregunta ___.
quiz.explanation: ¿Hace falta decir más? expects no reply, so it is a rhetorical question.
hints: It comes from the art of persuasion.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence fits a formal letter of condolence?
options: Lamentamos profundamente el fallecimiento de su padre.
Sentimos mucho que su padre haya estirado la pata.
¡Qué palo lo de su padre, de verdad!
quiz.correct_answer: Lamentamos profundamente el fallecimiento de su padre.
quiz.explanation: Fallecimiento is the formal euphemism for death. Estirar la pata and qué palo are colloquial and would jar badly in a condolence letter.
hints: Think of the register of the letter.

quiz.prompt: «Te lo he dicho un millón de veces.» Which device is this?
quiz.explanation: Nobody has said anything a million times. A deliberate exaggeration is a hyperbole, and it is at home in conversation.

quiz.prompt: Opposites set side by side, as in «rico en palabras, pobre en hechos», make an ___ (Spanish term).
quiz.explanation: Rico against pobre, palabras against hechos. Setting opposites against each other is an antithesis.

listening.text: No es poco, la verdad.
listening.meaning: It's no small thing, honestly.
listening.note: Litote: no es poco = it is a lot.

listening.text: Tu hermano no es ningún tonto.
listening.meaning: Your brother is no fool.

listening.text: Esta casa es un horno en agosto.
listening.meaning: This house is an oven in August.
listening.note: New word: el horno = the oven.

listening.text: ¿Hace falta recordar que el plazo terminó ayer?
listening.meaning: Do I need to remind you that the deadline was yesterday?
listening.note: A rhetorical question: nobody needs to answer.

listening.text: El jefe habla como si dictara a un notario.
listening.meaning: The boss talks as if he were dictating to a notary.
listening.note: New word: el notario = the notary.

listening.text: Sin coche, sin dinero y sin ganas, volvimos andando.
listening.meaning: With no car, no money and no will, we walked back.

listening.text: En una carta de pésame, falleció suena mejor que murió.
listening.meaning: In a condolence letter, passed away sounds better than died.

listening.text: Ganamos el partido por la mañana y perdimos el autobús por la tarde.
listening.meaning: We won the match in the morning and missed the bus in the afternoon.

guide.tip: To tell a metaphor from a simile, look for como, igual que or parecer. If the comparison word is there, it is a simile.

conversations.title: Cutting a speech down to size
conversations.scenario: Carmen, a speechwriter, goes through the speech that Julián, a city councillor, will give at the opening of a neighbourhood library.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Julián, he leído tu discurso. No está nada mal, pero sobra la mitad.
lines.meaning: Julián, I've read your speech. It's not bad at all, but half of it can go.
lines.note: Litote first, then the bad news.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿La mitad? Me he pasado tres noches escribiéndolo.
lines.meaning: Half? I spent three nights writing it.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Se nota. Empiezas cinco frases seguidas con queremos.
lines.meaning: It shows. You start five sentences in a row with 'we want'.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Es una anáfora. La repetición da fuerza, ¿no?
lines.meaning: It's an anaphora. Repetition gives strength, doesn't it?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tres veces, sí. Cinco suenan a mitin. Quédate con tres y cierra.
lines.meaning: Three times, yes. Five sound like a rally. Keep three and wrap up.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y lo de la biblioteca como faro del barrio?
lines.meaning: And the bit about the library as the lighthouse of the neighbourhood?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: La metáfora es bonita, pero ya la usaste el año pasado con la piscina.
lines.meaning: The metaphor is nice, but you already used it last year for the swimming pool.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Nadie se acordará. ¿O sí?
lines.meaning: Nobody will remember. Or will they?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Yo me acuerdo, y la prensa también. Mejor di que abre de nueve a nueve.
lines.meaning: I remember, and so does the press. Better to say it opens from nine to nine.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Y donde pongo recortes, ¿escribo ajuste presupuestario?
lines.meaning: And where I've got cuts, shall I write budget adjustment?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ni hablar. Ese eufemismo lo huele cualquiera. Di lo que hay y explica por qué.
lines.meaning: No way. Anyone can smell that euphemism. Say what's happening and explain why.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Entonces: menos adorno, más datos y una sola pregunta retórica al final.
lines.meaning: So: less ornament, more facts and a single rhetorical question at the end.

bites.title: Image or comparison
bites.rule: A metáfora says A is B (la reunión fue un pantano); a símil keeps como or igual que (como un pantano); a hipérbole exaggerates on purpose.

bites.title: Say less, mean more
bites.rule: The lítote denies the opposite: no es poco = it is a lot, no está nada mal = it is very good. The eufemismo softens a hard word: fallecer for morir.
bites.example: El resultado no está nada mal.

bites.title: Patterns
bites.rule: Anáfora repeats the opening word; quiasmo reverses a pair (A B, B A); antítesis sets opposites side by side; three parallel items close a thought.
bites.example: Sin prisa, sin ruido, sin miedo.
bites.example_meaning: No hurry, no noise, no fear.

bites.title: Right register
bites.rule: The register is culto, estándar or coloquial, and a device must fit its text. Hyperbole livens a chat and undermines a report; a euphemism comforts the bereaved and misleads in accounts.
bites.example: Lamentamos el fallecimiento de su madre.
bites.example_meaning: We are sorry for the passing of your mother.

sorts.title: Metaphor, simile or hyperbole?
sorts.why: Without a comparison word it is a metaphor. With como, igual que or parecer it is a simile. Deliberate exaggeration is hyperbole.

items.text: Tu despacho es una selva.
Su voz era un cuchillo.
Corre igual que un galgo.
Duerme como un tronco.
Tengo un millón de correos sin leer.
Me muero de sueño.

sorts.title: Says more, or says it softer?
sorts.why: A litote praises by denying the opposite; a euphemism softens an unwelcome fact.

items.text: No es poco.
No está nada mal.
No es ningún tonto.
persona mayor, for viejo
reajuste de plantilla, for despidos
pasar a mejor vida, for morir

sorts.title: Anaphora, chiasmus or antithesis?
sorts.why: Anaphora repeats the first word; chiasmus brings a pair back in reverse; antithesis sets opposites against each other.

items.text: Sin luz, sin agua, sin respuesta.
Cada día, cada hora, cada minuto.
Lo que dice, no lo hace; lo que hace, no lo dice.
Comemos tarde porque dormimos poco, y dormimos poco porque comemos tarde.
Mucho texto y poca idea.
Rico en palabras, pobre en hechos.

spots.sentence: Para elogiar el informe, dijo que no estaba nada bien.
spots.why: The praising litote is no está nada mal; no está nada bien means it is bad.

spots.sentence: Duerme como un tronco es un ejemplo de metáfora, porque compara con como.
spots.why: A comparison with como is a simile.

spots.sentence: Lamentamos profundamente que su abuelo palmara el martes.
spots.why: Palmar is colloquial for dying; a condolence message needs the formal fallecer.

spots.sentence: La anáfora repite la última palabra de cada frase.
spots.why: Anaphora repeats the opening word of each clause or line.

spots.sentence: En el quiasmo, los términos se repiten en orden idéntico.
spots.why: Chiasmus brings the pair back in reverse order: A B, B A.

builds.text: Tu propuesta no está nada mal.

builds.meaning: He spoke like someone counting coins.
Of that summer, little do I remember.

builds.text: ¿Quién no ha perdido nunca las llaves?
builds.meaning: Who has never lost their keys?

realm.content:
## La retórica en Eldmark

The chroniclers of Highgate love **hipérbole**: **el dragón tapó el sol durante una semana**. The dwarves of Deepanvil prefer the **lítote**: a mountain of gold **no está nada mal**. And every herald opens with an **anáfora**: **por el rey, por el reino, por el queso**.

vocabulary.example: Según la crónica, el dragón tapó el sol durante una semana: pura hipérbole.
vocabulary.example_meaning: According to the chronicle, the dragon blotted out the sun for a week: pure hyperbole.

vocabulary.example: Para un enano, una montaña de oro no está nada mal.
vocabulary.example_meaning: For a dwarf, a mountain of gold is not bad at all.

vocabulary.example: El heraldo abrió con una anáfora: por el rey, por el reino, por el queso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The herald opened with an anaphora: for the king, for the realm, for the cheese.

vocabulary.example: Para el cronista, aquel orco era un muro con hacha.
vocabulary.example_meaning: To the chronicler, that orc was a wall with an axe.

vocabulary.example: La maga llamó retirada estratégica a la huida: un eufemismo de manual.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage called the flight a strategic withdrawal: a textbook euphemism.

vocabulary.meaning: herald
vocabulary.example: El heraldo leyó el bando con voz de trueno.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The herald read the proclamation in a voice of thunder.

vocabulary.meaning: chronicler
vocabulary.example: El cronista exagera las victorias y olvida las derrotas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The chronicler exaggerates the victories and forgets the defeats.

vocabulary.meaning: chronicle
vocabulary.example: La crónica dedica tres páginas al almuerzo del rey.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The chronicle devotes three pages to the king's lunch.

bites.title: El heraldo
bites.rule: Eldmark's heralds open with an anáfora, its chroniclers inflate everything (hipérbole), and its dwarves praise by denying: no está nada mal.
bites.example: Por el rey, por el reino, por el queso.
bites.example_meaning: For the king, for the realm, for the cheese.

listening.text: El orco no es ningún cobarde.
listening.meaning: The orc is no coward.

listening.text: La crónica exagera, como siempre.
listening.meaning: The chronicle exaggerates, as always.

listening.text: El heraldo grita como una tormenta.
listening.meaning: The herald shouts like a storm.
listening.note: New word: el heraldo = the herald.

listening.text: El enano llamó paseo a la retirada.
listening.meaning: The dwarf called the retreat a stroll.
listening.note: New word: la retirada = the retreat.

listening.text: ¿Quién teme a un dragón dormido?
listening.meaning: Who is afraid of a sleeping dragon?

builds.text: Tu espada no está nada mal.
builds.meaning: Your sword is not bad at all.

builds.text: El paladín luchó como un oso.
builds.meaning: The paladin fought like a bear.

spots.sentence: El enano dijo que el tesoro no estaba nada bien, y sonrió.
spots.why: Praise by litote: no estaba nada mal.

spots.sentence: Llamar retirada estratégica a la huida es un ejemplo de hipérbole.
spots.why: It softens the fact instead of exaggerating it, so it is a euphemism.

sorts.title: Images in the chronicle
sorts.why: Without a comparison word it is a metaphor. With como or igual que it is a simile. Deliberate exaggeration is hyperbole.

items.text: El orco era un muro.
La elfa era una flecha en el bosque.
El minotauro corre como un carro.
La maga brilla igual que una antorcha.
El cazador come por diez guerreros.
El enano lleva mil años sin sonreír.

quiz.prompt: La crónica dice: «El dragón bostezó y se apagaron todas las antorchas de Highgate.» Which device?
quiz.explanation: A yawn that puts out every torch in a city is a deliberate exaggeration. That is hyperbole, the chronicler's favourite.
hints: Could a yawn really do that?

quiz.prompt: A dwarf's highest praise, by litote: Cien monedas de oro no son ___.
quiz.explanation: No son pocas denies the opposite to mean 'they are a lot'. That is a litote. Pocas agrees with monedas, feminine plural.

meadowbrook.content:
## La retórica en Meadowbrook

The Meadowbrook almanac writes in **metáforas**: **la helada es una ladrona que entra sin llamar**. At the tavern, Leo the fisherman lives on **hipérbole**: **pesqué un pez más grande que la barca**. And Rosa praises a pumpkin with a **lítote**: **no está nada mal**.

vocabulary.example: Para el almanaque, la helada es una ladrona que entra sin llamar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: To the almanac, frost is a thief who comes in without knocking.

vocabulary.example: Leo jura que pescó un pez más grande que la barca.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo swears he caught a fish bigger than the boat.

vocabulary.example: Rosa miró la calabaza de Nora y dijo que no estaba nada mal.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa looked at Nora's pumpkin and said it wasn't bad at all.

vocabulary.example: Las ovejas bajaron del monte como nubes con patas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The sheep came down the hill like clouds with legs.

vocabulary.example: ¿Quién no ha soñado con ganar el festival? Es la pregunta retórica de cada primavera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Who hasn't dreamt of winning the festival? It's every spring's rhetorical question.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde llama cosecha modesta a un desastre: es su eufemismo favorito.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor calls a disaster a modest harvest: it's his favourite euphemism.

vocabulary.meaning: almanac
vocabulary.example: El almanaque predice un invierno largo y una primavera generosa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The almanac predicts a long winter and a generous spring.

vocabulary.meaning: fisherman
vocabulary.example: El pescador cuenta sus historias con mucha hipérbole.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The fisherman tells his stories with plenty of hyperbole.

vocabulary.meaning: frost
vocabulary.example: La helada llegó sin avisar y se llevó las fresas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The frost came without warning and took the strawberries.

bites.title: El almanaque
bites.rule: The almanac paints with metáforas, Leo exaggerates (hipérbole) and Rosa praises by denying the opposite (lítote). A pumpkin that no está nada mal is a fine one.
bites.example: Esta calabaza no está nada mal.

listening.text: Las fresas no están nada mal.
listening.meaning: The strawberries are pretty good.

listening.text: La vaca camina como una reina.
listening.meaning: The cow walks like a queen.

listening.text: El otoño es el pintor del bosque.
listening.meaning: Autumn is the forest's painter.

listening.text: Según el almanaque, el invierno durará mil años.
listening.meaning: According to the almanac, winter will last a thousand years.
listening.note: New word: el almanaque = the almanac.

listening.text: ¿Quién no ha perdido una gallina alguna vez?
listening.meaning: Who hasn't lost a hen at some point?

builds.text: Tu maíz no está nada mal.
Las ovejas parecen nubes con patas.
builds.meaning: The sheep look like clouds with legs.

spots.sentence: Leo pescó un pez del tamaño de una ballena, y lo llama lítote.
spots.why: A fish the size of a whale is an exaggeration, so it is hyperbole.

spots.sentence: El almanaque dice que la helada es una ladrona: un bonito ejemplo de símil.
spots.why: There is no como. The frost simply is a thief, which is a metaphor.

sorts.title: Litote or hyperbole at the farm?
sorts.why: A litote says more by denying the opposite; a hyperbole says more by exaggerating.

items.text: Tu maíz no está nada mal.
Leo no es ningún mal pescador.
La fiesta no fue poca cosa.
Tengo un millón de fresas que cosechar.
Esta calabaza pesa una tonelada.
Llevo un siglo esperando la lluvia.

quiz.prompt: El almanaque: «En marzo, la tierra se despierta y bosteza.» Which device?
quiz.explanation: The earth does not really wake up or yawn: it is an image with no comparison word, a metaphor (here, a personification).

quiz.prompt: Leo turns his metaphor into a simile: El pez era grande ___ una barca.
quiz.explanation: Como (or igual que) makes the comparison visible: a simile.

conversations.title: A notice for the almanac
conversations.scenario: Nora, the new farmer, and Rosa from the seed shop write the festival notice for the Meadowbrook almanac.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Rosa, el alcalde quiere un texto sobre el festival para el almanaque.
lines.meaning: Rosa, the mayor wants a piece about the festival for the almanac.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Otra vez? ¿Y qué ha escrito él?
lines.meaning: Again? And what has he written?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Dice que nuestras calabazas son las más grandes del universo.
lines.meaning: He says our pumpkins are the biggest in the universe.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Hipérbole de alcalde. Mejor algo con gracia: nuestras calabazas no están nada mal.
lines.meaning: Mayor's hyperbole. Better something with charm: our pumpkins aren't bad at all.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Y si añadimos tres cosas: música, fresas y baile?
lines.meaning: And what if we add three things: music, strawberries and dancing?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Perfecto. Tres suenan a fiesta; cinco, a lista de la compra.
lines.meaning: Perfect. Three sound like a party; five, like a shopping list.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Y terminamos con una pregunta: ¿quién se va a quedar en casa?
lines.meaning: And we finish with a question: who's going to stay at home?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Nadie, claro. Por eso es retórica.
lines.meaning: Nobody, of course. That's why it's rhetorical.

rustwake.content:
## La retórica en el páramo

The wasteland's radio bulletin is pure rhetoric. The weather is an **eufemismo** (**hay un poco de polvo**, during an ash storm), the market's adverts are **hipérbole** (**la gaseosa Zafiro más fría del universo**), and Marta's reviews are **lítotes**: **esta armadura no está nada mal**.

vocabulary.example: El boletín llama un poco de polvo a una tormenta de ceniza: menudo eufemismo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The bulletin calls an ash storm a bit of dust: some euphemism.

vocabulary.example: Marta anuncia la gaseosa Zafiro más fría del universo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta advertises the coldest Zafiro soda in the universe.

vocabulary.example: Leo probó la armadura de chatarra y dijo que no estaba nada mal.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo tried on the scrap armour and said it wasn't bad at all.

vocabulary.example: Cada boletín empieza igual: atención, páramo; atención, cúpula; atención, buscadores.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Every bulletin starts the same way: attention, plains; attention, Dome; attention, scavengers.

vocabulary.example: ¿Quién necesita la cúpula con tanto polvo gratis? La pregunta retórica hace reír a todo el mercado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Who needs the Dome with so much free dust? The rhetorical question makes the whole market laugh.

vocabulary.meaning: bulletin
vocabulary.example: El boletín de la mañana dura dos minutos y promete tres tormentas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The morning bulletin lasts two minutes and promises three storms.

vocabulary.meaning: announcer, radio presenter
vocabulary.example: El locutor habla como un motor que no quiere arrancar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The announcer talks like an engine that won't start.

vocabulary.meaning: advert, announcement
vocabulary.example: Cada anuncio del mercado promete agua filtrada para mil años.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Every market advert promises filtered water for a thousand years.

bites.title: Radio del páramo
bites.rule: The bulletin softens the weather (eufemismo: un poco de polvo), inflates the adverts (hipérbole) and praises by denying (lítote: no está nada mal).
bites.example: Hoy hay un poco de polvo en el páramo.
bites.example_meaning: There is a little dust on the plains today.

listening.text: La armadura no está nada mal.
listening.meaning: The armour is not bad at all.

listening.text: El locutor habla como un motor viejo.
listening.meaning: The announcer talks like an old engine.
listening.note: New word: el locutor = the announcer.

listening.text: Hoy hay un poco de ceniza, nada más.
listening.meaning: There's a little ash today, that's all.

listening.text: El anuncio promete tuercas para toda la vida.
listening.meaning: The advert promises nuts for life.
listening.note: New word: el anuncio = the advert.

listening.text: ¿Quién quiere volver a la cúpula?
listening.meaning: Who wants to go back to the Dome?

builds.text: Este tónico no está nada mal.
builds.meaning: This tonic is not bad at all.

builds.text: La radio cruje como una puerta vieja.
builds.meaning: The radio creaks like an old door.

spots.sentence: El boletín llama un poco de polvo a la tormenta: un ejemplo de hipérbole.
spots.why: It makes the storm sound smaller, not bigger, so it is a euphemism.

spots.sentence: El anuncio dice que la gaseosa Zafiro es la más fría del universo: pura lítote.
spots.why: The coldest in the universe is an exaggeration, so it is hyperbole.

sorts.title: What is the bulletin doing?
sorts.why: A euphemism shrinks bad news, a hyperbole inflates good news, a litote praises by denying the opposite.

items.text: un poco de polvo, for an ash storm
un escarabajo algo grande, for a giant beetle
agua filtrada para mil años
la tienda más barata del universo
El tónico no está nada mal.
El robot no es ningún tonto.

quiz.prompt: Boletín: «Leve brisa de ceniza en el páramo; recomendamos no salir en tres días.» What softens the news?
quiz.explanation: A breeze that keeps you indoors for three days is a storm, so leve brisa is a euphemism.
hints: Would you stay in for three days because of a breeze?

quiz.prompt: The bulletin's anaphora: Atención, buscadores; atención, mercaderes; ___, capataz.
quiz.explanation: Anaphora repeats the opening word of each phrase, here atención three times.
hints: The word every phrase starts with.
